To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the dislocations forming regular arrays in Si are undissociated and their intersections form extended point defects with the symmetry depending on the boundary type.
(a/2)(110) screw dislocations in silicon form regular two-dimensional arrays with characteristic extended point defect structures at the intersections of screw dislocations.

(1) the dislocations are undissociated; (2) the dislocation core is formed by a closed loop of atoms; (3) the core structure is different at intersections of dislocations forming a twist or a tilt boundary; (4) the dislocation intersection core is formed by an extended point defect (a closed loop of atoms).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the atomic structure of extended defects formed by dislocation intersections in Si.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the screw dislocations forming the (001) twist and shear boundaries are dissociated in a similar way, but their intersections are characterized by different extended point defect structures.
the atomic configurations of the screw dislocation intersections in silicon depend on the type of the boundary they generate.

the dislocation intersections in the twist boundary are composed of the extended point defects, which are formed by 12 atoms in a characteristic configuration of a regular octahedron with the edge length of 1.5 nm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the atomic structure of the dislocation intersection is determined by the local stress field of the dislocations and is independent on the dislocation line directions.
the screw dislocations in the Si(001) twist boundaries are dissociated and that the dissociation occurs in the form of the extended point defect configurations.

the screw dislocation intersections form extended point defects with the symmetry of the intersection, i.e., the symmetry of the point group of the dislocation network, which are characterized by an excess number of atoms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the atomic configurations of the extended point defects are not determined by the dislocation character, but rather by the boundary type.
the atomic structure of the dislocation intersection cores in the (001) twist boundary differs significantly from that in the (001)(110) shear boundary.
extended point defect structures are a general feature of dislocation intersections in silicon and other covalent crystals, and they can be used as markers for dislocation imaging in HREM.
